item.title: L'Exemplaire – Émie Lanteigne, Victor Marchand et Imelda Njiki : Hockey junior : le retour de la Russie fait toujours débat
item.dc:creator: Émie Lanteigne, Victor Marchand et Imelda Njiki
item.description: La Russie demeure exclue du prochain Championnat du monde junior de hockey des moins de 20 ans, malgré une ordonnance du Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS). Plusieurs pays s'opposent toujours à sa réintégration dans les compétitions internationales, notamment en raison du contexte politique international. Depuis l’invasion de l’Ukraine en février 2022, les instances sportives internationales naviguent en eaux troubles entre neutralité politique et sanctions géopolitiques. Fin octobre 2026, un coup de théâtre juridique a ravivé les tensions dans le monde du hockey : le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) a ordonné la réintégration immédiate des équipes russes et biélorusses dans les compétitions internationales. Pourtant, entre blocages frontaliers, révolte des pays hôtes et soupçons de conflits d’intérêts, le retour de la Russie sur la glace est aujourd’hui dans une impasse totale.

item.title: The Link – Lisa Mizan: Concordia University at a crossroads
item.dc:creator: Lisa Mizan
item.description: In 2023, the province's English-language universities became another front in the debate when the government announced it would raise tuition for new Canadian students from outside the province attending English-language universities. The hikes resulted in increases up to $12,000 a year, up from about $9,000. The increase took effect in fall 2024. International students have also faced substantially higher costs due to federal tuition increases, and former Quebec Premier François Legault defended the changes as part of a broader effort to rebalance the province’s university system and strengthen French-language institutions.

item.title: The Link – Oliver Richman: A look ahead to Concordia’s 2026-2027 basketball seasons
item.dc:creator: Oliver Richman
item.description: After finishing second that season in the Réseau du sport étudiant du Québec (RSEQ), the Stingers were given a wild card spot in the Final 8 national tournament hosted by the University of British Columbia (UBC). Concordia would go on to upset RSEQ rival Bishop’s University as well as UBC to take fifth place in the tournament. Unfortunately for Concordia, injuries and close losses riddled their promising 2025-26 campaign. They were able to scrape together a 10-9 record in the regular season, good enough for a third-place RSEQ finish. The Stingers would go on to lose to the Université Laval Rouge et Or in the semifinals of the playoffs, missing out on the national tournament.

item.title: The Link – James Bossinakis: Canada proposes indefinite exclusion for people with mental illnesses seeking MAID
item.dc:creator: James Bossinakis
item.description: In October 2026, the Canadian government introduced Bill C-41, the Medical Assistance in Dying Safeguards Act. The legislation aims to amend Criminal Code regulations around who is eligible for medical assistance in dying (MAID) in Canada. The proposed legislation would affect citizens seeking MAID for mental illness as the sole reason and indefinitely postpone the end of a 2021 exclusion under Bill C-7 that was set to expire next March. The federal government cited serious concerns over safety and the potential for inconsistency in judging which cases are in temporary crisis and which are terminal.

item.title: The Link – Marissa Guthrie: Albertan students reflect on referendum
item.dc:creator: Marissa Guthrie
item.description: Alberta hosted a vote on the possibility of a referendum on Oct. 19, with the results dictating that the province will remain in Canada and an official referendum on sovereignty will not take place. Quebec has held two referendums on sovereignty, first in 1980 and then again in 1995, when the population voted to remain in Canada by one per cent. The Parti Québécois (PQ) won the provincial election in October, with one of its campaign objectives being to host another referendum in the coming years.

item.title: The Link – Sana Paracha: Uniting from al-Maghreb to ash-Shām to celebrate Palestinian culture
item.dc:creator: Sana Paracha
item.description: On Nov. 22, Concordia University’s Palestinian Cultural Club (PCC) held the North Africa United for Palestine fundraising gala. The event featured Arabic music, a packed dance floor with the occasional dabke circle, Moroccan food from sponsors and homemade dishes. The event was a collaboration between several clubs from McGill University and Université de Montréal, such as the Algerian Students’ Association, Moroccan Students’ Association, Tunisian Student Society and the Comité des étudiants maghrébins de l’UdeM. The proceeds from the event, which was nearly sold out, will go directly to support the activities of Islamic Relief Canada and Doctors Without Borders in Palestine.

item.title: The Link: Editorial: The strike is student-led; the struggle is popular
item.dc:creator: The Link
item.description: The province-wide strikes were organized by the Coalition de résistance pour l’unité étudiante syndicale (CRUES) and lasted from Nov. 9 to Nov. 13. On Nov. 10, students held a sit-in at Concordia University’s Henry F. Hall Building, and on Nov. 13, thousands of students took to the streets of Montreal. These events did not come out of the blue. They were born out of years of provincial neglect and deliberate policy choices targeting post-secondary schools. Last year, Quebec’s network of 48 CEGEPs reported that they were facing a combined $150 million shortfall. This report came after the Quebec government announced it would reduce its financing for the 2025-2026 school year.

item.title: The Link – Kara Brulotte: Cancel culture is a monster of our own creation
item.dc:creator: Kara Brulotte
item.description: Cancel culture has become Frankenstein's monster, killing its own creator. What began as a way to hold people accountable has devolved into community infighting, undermining movements and ignoring the root of the issue. It didn’t start out this way. Cancelling people originated in Black and queer communities, eventually making its way onto Twitter as a way to hold the rich and powerful accountable in the court of social media public opinion. It was a way to take back power in situations where a court of law would never try the guilty party.

item.title: The Link – Jaiden Gales: You can’t save the whole world
item.dc:creator: Jaiden Gales
item.description: Online platforms amplify attention-grabbing content, making every crisis feel urgent and constant, while some critique those who aren’t actively fighting for a better world every second of the day. It can be hard to draw the line between meaningful concern and simply making ourselves suffer along with the rest of the world. We’re pressured to feel like we should. It isn’t a bad thing to care about the world’s well-being, and it’s normal to feel overwhelmed by humanity’s suffering. As humans, we’re wired with a desire to help. This is a good thing, but it's best accomplished with a community and is not very productive alone.

item.title: The Link – Eliza Lee: It’s time to put zines and journalism on the same page
item.dc:creator: Eliza Lee
item.description: Through this friend, I was first introduced to the wonderful world of zines: self-published, DIY booklets about anything from recipes for the clinically depressed to deep-dives on the women of Gilmore Girls. Thanks to my roommate, one part of my bookcase is now dedicated to zines of all colours and sizes amongst magazines and student papers I’ve accumulated. Initially, it might seem strange to put journalistic work and zines side-by-side. But my studies in journalism, and my roommate’s in fine arts, have taught us that zines have long been a legitimate form of citizen journalism.

item.title: The Link – Aïda M. Lopes: Quebec’s video game industry wants to reclaim its space in cultural circles
item.dc:creator: Aïda M. Lopes
item.description: Quebec’s video game industry generates $1.4 billion in annual revenues, according to La Guilde du jeu vidéo du Québec. Yet local talent feels left out of cultural conversations. To bring more attention to locally developed games, industry members gathered at Ausgang Plaza on St-Hubert St. on Nov. 14 for the inaugural Buy a Quebec Video Game Day, held as part of Festival Gros Joueurs. Gamers in the city have likely already bought local games, but they might not know it. Making sure they have that knowledge is the mission of gamesfromquebec.com, a website showcasing local expertise launched by La Guilde.

item.title: The Concordian – Eric Klempan: Concordia launches new Sustainability Action Plan, outlining green goals for the next four years
item.dc:creator: Eric Klempan
item.description: This semester, Concordia University launched its 2026-30 Sustainability Action Plan (SAP). The strategy outlines sustainability goals to be achieved over the next four years, focusing on five operational streams: climate, biodiversity, procurement, food and waste. The plan also includes the engagement streams of curriculum and research. Overall, the new goals follow those of the 2020-25 strategy, with the biggest additions being the procurement and biodiversity streams. According to the final progress report of the last SAP, only 72 per cent of targets and 62 per cent of strategies were completed, leaving many initiatives to be completed in the current plan.

item.title: The Concordian – Aidan Flanagan: The 69th Grammy Awards nominations boast inconsistency
item.dc:creator: Aidan Flanagan
item.description: While every year’s nominations look different, one constant remains: the results are met with a mixture of praise, criticism and, more often, confusion. Categories like Best New Artist have been met with the latter, while many nominees in the “Big Three” categories have been received largely well. Record of the Year, Album of the Year and Song of the Year, consisted of names that made sense. Olivia Dean, Olivia Rodrigo and the ever-present Taylor Swift have all appeared with their respective chart-topping songs.

item.title: The Concordian – Anna Dunlop: QUICKSPIN: U2 — Carnaval de Luz
item.dc:creator: Anna Dunlop
item.description: While it makes bold attempts that don’t suit the band’s style and leans into desperate alignments with youth, the record unfortunately can’t settle on one coherent style or sound. It keeps shifting its tone and genre, but it still shows self-awareness and genuine admiration for a long career. The album starts off strong, with a high-energy, nostalgic sound in both “Go (Carnaval de Luz)” and “La Reina.” However, it quickly loses its footing over the next five tracks, becoming slightly overproduced as certain hooks lean toward changing-room music.

item.title: The Concordian – Aidan Flanagan: QUICKSPIN: Snoh Aalegra — Legendary Love
item.dc:creator: Aidan Flanagan
item.description: Snoh Aalegra has been a long-time favourite among modern R&B fans for her ability to blend the genre’s past and future. Her smoky vocals are reminiscent of an old soul and are often paired with more modern instrumentals. Yet on her first full-length release in five years, Aalegra fully leans into the old R&B days in what will likely become a seminal work in her discography. Legendary Love triumphs in exploring heartbreak and hope for what could have been. “Run Free” opens the album like an ‘80s soul track with warm synths and mid-tempo drums. Synths are consistent throughout this record, drawing endless inspiration from ‘80s pop, soul and neo-soul.

item.title: The Concordian – Kim Bouchard: La place des femmes en photojournalisme : qui a la chance de raconter le monde en images?
item.dc:creator: Kim Bouchard
item.description: En cette session d’automne qui touche à sa fin, je m’apprête à terminer, dans quelques mois, un programme de deuxième cycle en journalisme visuel à l’Université Concordia. Comme plusieurs personnes étudiantes de mon âge, je me demande où j’aboutirai à la fin de mon parcours académique. Mais une chose est certaine : ce que je souhaite profondément, c’est devenir photojournaliste. Ce qui me préoccupe toutefois, c’est mon avenir dans cette profession en tant que femme, et en tant que femme issue d’une minorité visible. Quelle sera ma place dans un domaine, encore aujourd’hui, largement dominé par les hommes? Cette inquiétude m’amène à me poser des questions qui dépassent mon propre futur : Qui a accès à la production et à la narration des histoires visuelles dans les médias d’information? Quels points de vue et quelles réalités y sont représentés visuellement?

item.title: The Link – Nicolas Tremblay: SPVM arrests two former Montreal police officers
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Tremblay
item.description: Montreal police (SPVM) arrested two former officers on Nov. 21 for alleged discriminatory and racist acts. Both officers were from Station 39 and were part of the seven police officers fired earlier this month, according to the SPVM. Five of the officers were from Station 39, and two were from Station 21, according to SPVM Chief Fady Dagher. They were let go due to allegations of racism, discrimination and misconduct. The two former officers from Station 39 were arrested following a warrant issued by the Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions (DPCP) and face charges of assault, criminal harassment and breach of trust, according to Montreal police.

item.title: Le Club-École – Theo Lopes Fernandes : Deux équipes couronnées championnes au soccer sud-américain
item.dc:creator: Theo Lopes Fernandes
item.description: Deux compétitions sud-américaines ont vu un vainqueur désigné cette fin de semaine. Six fois champions d’Amérique, Boca Juniors a remporté son premier titre international depuis 2008. Au championnat brésilien, le Flamengo a décroché le titre après un match décisif contre le seul adversaire qui pouvait encore le dépasser dans le classement. Le club argentin ramène, pour la troisième fois de son histoire, la Copa Sudamericana à Buenos Aires. Depuis la Recopa sud-américaine de 2008, le Boca Juniors n’avait remporté aucun trophée international. La Copa Sudamericana est l’équivalent de la Ligue Europa en Amérique du sud. Le vainqueur obtient également une place en phase de groupe de la Libertadores de l’année suivante.

item.title: Quartier Libre – Jeanne Le Goff : Archivistique : Étudier le passé comme carrière d’avenir
item.dc:creator: Jeanne Le Goff
item.description: Les étudiant·e·s en archivistique entament leurs études sous le signe de l’incertitude. La multiplication des coupes budgétaires dans les institutions et l’essor du numérique transforment en profondeur leur futur métier, forçant une réinvention de celui-ci. Pour mieux comprendre cette réalité, Quartier Libre est allé à leur rencontre, ainsi qu’à celle de spécialistes du secteur. Bien qu’il soit aujourd’hui en pleine évolution, le métier d’archiviste a longtemps souffert d’une image stéréotypée. « Traditionnellement, les archivistes ont toujours eu l’image vieillotte d’une personne qui est dans le fond de son sous-sol et attend qu’il y ait des visiteurs ou des chercheurs qui viennent consulter ses archives », explique l’experte-conseil en gestion de l’information dans le domaine de l’éducation Florence Rousseau.

item.title: The Link – Trent Deschamps-Coinner: The many controversies of the 2026 WNBA season
item.dc:creator: Trent Deschamps-Coinner
item.description: The 2026 Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA) season was another reminder that sports and politics are impossible to separate. Fans only enjoyed a couple of months of pure hoops during the 2026 season before the league became a centre of culture-war discussion points and right-wing political grifting. The season took place on the heels of a long negotiation surrounding the collective bargaining agreement between the WNBA Players’ Union and the league. There was a real possibility that the players would have gone on strike, potentially disrupting the season. However, last March, WNBA players unanimously voted to accept a new seven-year collective bargaining agreement, and the WNBA season proceeded as scheduled, tipping off May 8, 2026.

item.title: La Pige – Olivier Dubois : La coupe ou rien : les coulisses d’une conquête inoubliable
item.dc:creator: Olivier Dubois
item.description: Les émotions derrière la conquête du trophée Gilles-Courteau sont revenues à la surface au Cinéma Odyssée. item.title: The Link – Eve Learns: What went wrong with the McGill Law controversy
item.dc:creator: Eve Learns
item.description: He was convicted of second-degree murder and attempted murder for two violent attacks committed in British Columbia in 1984. Eventually, his criminal past became known among the student body, which resulted in some students anonymously reaching out to the CBC. Shortly thereafter, other news outlets began reporting on the story, which further sensationalized an already controversial issue. Over the weekend of Oct. 16 to Oct. 18, CTV, the Montreal Gazette and La Presse all came out with their own article on the “McGill murderer,” further pressuring McGill for a response.
